summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, coronary artery disease, and congestive heart failure, was admitted for acute chest pain and shortness of breath following cocaine use and missed dialysis. Imaging revealed a large right pleural effusion and pulmonary edema due to fluid overload. He underwent therapeutic thoracentesis, which improved his symptoms, and received hemodialysis to manage volume status. During the hospitalization, he was diagnosed with Clostridium difficile infection, likely triggered by recent antibiotics, and was started on appropriate treatment. His heart failure was optimized with medication adjustments. He expressed interest in addiction counseling before discharge. He was discharged stable with plans to resume dialysis, continue C. diff treatment, and follow up with primary care, psychiatry, and addiction services.
